newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX gasoline sharpens losses on Trainer restart.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX gasoline sharpens losses on Trainer restart.

text.p: NYMEX gasoline sharpened losses Thursday midday after Tosco Corp said it reopened its Trainer, Pennsylvania refinery which will add about 100,000 barrels a day of gasoline to the market.
"We came off some more on the announcement, but in a way it is old news because we have been expecting it for so long. The selling is not very aggressive," said a New York gasoline trader.
At 1239 EDT, June gasoline was off 0.38 cent at 64.00 cents a gallon after falling as low as 63.75 cents.
The Trainer refinery had been shut since early 1996 for a $50 million modernization after Tosco acquired the plant from British Petroleum.
Tosco had said the official restart would be mid-May and dealers had known the refinery, which has total capacity of 150,000 barrels per day, was being tested by Tosco this week.

By 1300 EDT, news that Phillips Petroleum Co said its 205,000 barrel per day Sweeny, Texas refinery was shut for three to seven days pushed June gasoline up from its lower levels, down only 0.13 cent at 64.25 cents a gallon.
Philips said the refinery was shut due to a power outage in the refinery's local area.
Crude and heating oil mimicked gasoline's price action dipping further and then retracing losses on the news events.
"We went down ten more cents and then erased the losses. The news cancelled each other out" said a New York crude trader.
June crude stood five cents lower at $21.34 a barrel after falling to $21.18 a barrel while June heating oil was up 0.08 cent a gallon at 56.50 cents after falling to 55.90 cents.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
